presentation.label: Asthma (acute episode)
presentation.free_text_prompt: Tell us about your asthma symptoms and when they started.

questions.question: Do you have a diagnosis of asthma?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has a diagnosis of asthma?

questions.question: Are you feeling short of breath at rest, or unable to speak in full sentences?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient is short of breath at rest or unable to speak in full sentences?
questions.pdf_label: SOB at rest / cannot complete sentences

questions.question: Are your lips or face turning blue?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has cyanosis (blue lips or face)?

questions.question: Have you used your reliever (blue) inhaler in the last few hours?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has used their reliever inhaler in the last few hours?

questions.question: Is your reliever inhaler giving you less relief than usual, or wearing off more quickly?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient's reliever inhaler is giving less relief than usual or wearing off more quickly?

questions.question: How many puffs of your reliever inhaler have you needed today?
questions.range_warning_text: This is a higher number of puffs than expected. If you have needed significantly more reliever than usual, please seek urgent medical advice.

questions.question: Have you woken up at night because of your asthma symptoms?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has woken at night because of asthma symptoms?

questions.question: Is your asthma limiting your ability to do your normal daily activities?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient's asthma is limiting their normal daily activities?

questions.question: Have you had a cough, cold, or chest infection recently?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has had a recent cough, cold, or chest infection that may have triggered their asthma?

questions.question: Have you had chest pain?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has had chest pain?

questions.question: Have you had a fever?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has had a fever?

questions.question: Have you ever been admitted to hospital or needed steroid tablets for your asthma?
questions.encoder_prompt: Does the response indicate that the patient has previously been admitted to hospital or needed oral steroids for their asthma?

questions.question: How long have you had these symptoms?

severe_breathlessness_safety.message: This form is for routine issues and it may take several days to receive a response. If you are struggling to breathe, unable to speak in full sentences, or your lips or face are turning blue, this is a medical emergency - call 999 or go to A&E immediately.

reduced_reliever_response_safety.message: This form is for routine issues and it may take several days to receive a response. If your reliever inhaler is not helping as much as usual, phone the duty doctor or NHS 111 instead of submitting this form.
